Last Thursday (Nov 12) the ingestion pipeline stalled for 3h40, from 08:47 to 12:27 UTC. Customer dashboards showed stale data; events kept arriving in Kafka and were only processed late. No customer data was lost. [1]

What broke: ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB and shipped to every pod at once. With a 512 Mi memory limit, ingest-worker pods OOM-looped on the first large batch and crash-looped. [1][3] There was no consumer-lag alert; the first signal was a Sentry out-of-memory alert at 09:14, 27 minutes after the deploy. An early guess about Kafka broker disk was ruled out at 09:41 (disk at 62%). [1][3] Rollback to v2.13.3 finished at 10:05; lag drained by 12:27. [1] A Nov 13 reconciliation confirmed no events were lost, and Maya told Orbitly the same. [1][2]

What is changing:
- ingest#419 (merged Nov 13, shipped as v2.14.1 via canary) puts the default back to 1 MB, refuses a batch larger than 25% of the container memory limit, and keeps 10 MB only for the bulk-import path on the 2 Gi pool. [12]
- KES-431: page on-call when consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (Noa, due Nov 20). [1]
- KES-432: ingest config changes go to the canary pool first (Daniel, due Nov 27). [1]
- KES-433: raise the worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes (Lior, due Nov 27). [1]
